transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doc. Well, what brings me in is... I just hardly eat right anymore. Some days it's really just coffee and, I don't know, maybe a piece of bread. And my pants are just hanging loose on me now. I figured I should come see someone about it.
When you're not eating much, is it because you've lost your appetite and don't feel hungry, or is there another reason — like you're feeling sad or down, or you just don't feel like doing things?

I guess it's... well, it's more that I'm feeling down. Most days I just wake up with this heavy, empty feeling right in my chest. It's like nothing good is waiting for me, so I just want to keep my head down. When I feel like that all day, eating just doesn't even cross my mind.
Have you experienced periods like this before — times when you felt this way for weeks or months — or is this the first time you're going through something like this?

I'm not exactly sure about other times, but... well, this depressed spell I'm in right now, it's been hanging over me for about five months now. Yeah, it's been about five months of just feeling like this.
Before this five-month period that started about five months ago, have you ever had another time in your life when you felt depressed or down like this for weeks or months at a stretch?

I don't think so. I mean... I can't really remember feeling this bad before. You know, everyone has a bad day here or there, but... nothing that lasted for weeks or months at a time. As far as I know, it's just been this one stretch right now.

I want to make sure I have this right — looking back over your whole life before these past five months, have you ever had a stretch of time, even a few weeks, where you felt noticeably sad or depressed, or lost interest in things you normally enjoy?

No, I... I really haven't. I know you're just making sure, but yeah, looking back over everything... it's really just been these last five months. Before this started, I never went through a time where I felt this down or stopped caring about things for weeks at a stretch. It's just this one time.
Have you ever had a stretch of time, even just a few days, where you felt unusually energetic, optimistic, or 'up' — maybe needing less sleep than usual or feeling like you could do anything?

Yeah, actually... there was a time like that. Right after I got fired, I didn't feel down about it at first. I actually felt really fired up. Like I was just... kind of untouchable, you know? But I was also getting mad pretty easy. Like, if anyone told me I should slow down, I would just snap at them real fast.
When you felt that fired-up, energetic way after getting fired — was that before these five months of depression started, or did it happen during these past five months?

I... I'm not really sure, to be honest. I just know it was right after I lost my job. But trying to figure out if that was right before these last five months of feeling down started, or if it was already during... I don't know. My head's a bit foggy with the exact dates, so I couldn't tell you for sure.

Let me ask this a different way to help clarify the timeline. When you lost your job and felt that fired-up, energetic way with the irritability — roughly how long ago did that happen? Was it around 5 months ago, or was it longer ago than that?

I... I really can't say for sure. I know it was after I got fired, but trying to pin down exactly how many months ago that was... I just don't know. Everything kind of blurs together. I'm sorry, I just can't remember if it was around five months ago or longer.

When you felt that fired-up and irritable way after losing your job, did that happen before you started feeling the heavy, empty chest feeling that's been going on for five months — or did those two feelings start around the same time?

I just... I really can't say. I don't know if the fired-up feeling happened before the empty chest feeling started, or if they kind of hit at the same time. It's all just a jumble in my head right now. I'm sorry, I just don't know.

When you think back to that time right after you got fired when you felt fired up and irritable — was that feeling already going away before the heavy, empty chest feeling started, or did you still feel that way when the depression began?

I... I really don't know. Like I said, it's all just a blur. I can't remember if the fired-up feeling stopped before the heavy feeling started, or if they overlapped. I just... I can't keep the timeline straight in my head. I'm sorry.

Right now, today, do you still feel that fired-up, energetic, irritable way that you felt after losing your job — or has that feeling completely gone away and been replaced by the heavy, empty chest feeling?
No, I don't feel that fired-up way right now. It's... it's gone. Today, it's just that heavy, empty feeling in my chest. That's all I feel right now.

When you first started feeling that heavy, empty chest feeling about five months ago — had you already stopped feeling the fired-up and irritable way by that point, or were you still feeling fired up when the depression first hit?

I just... I honestly can't give you a clear answer on that either. I know you're trying to figure out the exact order of things, but my memory of that time is just really messed up. I don't know if the irritable feeling was completely gone when the emptiness started, or if they kind of crossed paths. It's just too fuzzy to say for sure.
When you were feeling fired up and irritable after losing your job, did that feeling last for just a few days, or did it go on for a week or more before it went away?

I don't know... I really can't say how long it lasted. Like I said, that whole time is just a blur to me. I can't remember if it was a few days or a week or longer. I'm sorry, I just don't have a good sense of time for back then.

In these past five months while you've been feeling that heavy, empty chest feeling — have you had any days or weeks where you felt that fired-up, energetic, irritable way again, or has it stayed completely gone the whole time?

No, it's... it's stayed completely gone. Since that heavy feeling started, I haven't had any of that fired-up energy at all. It's just been the emptiness, every day. None of that irritability or energy has come back.
